attempts.label: DANDI:001256
attempts.paper_title: Cortical Zinc Signaling Is Necessary for Changes in Mouse Pupil Diameter That Are Evoked by Background Sounds with Different Contrasts
attempts.entry_title: Cortical zinc and sound-contrast pupil responses (Cody, Kumar and Tzounopoulos 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Cody, Kumar and Tzounopoulos (2024) on dandiset 001256, which holds two-photon imaging of auditory cortex and pupillometry in 30 mice during low- and high-contrast sound, before and after ZX1 or ACSF, in C57BL6/J, ZnT3-WT and ZnT3-KO mice. It tests how pure-tone responses and contrast gain control vary with baseline pupil size, whether evoked pupil responses depend on contrast and on cortical zinc, and the controls of Figure 6. The widefield experiments of Figure 5 are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Peak pure-tone responses of A1 principal cells, contrasts combined, vary with baseline PD in an inverse U, largest at intermediate baseline PD (Kruskal-Wallis p = 5.91e-7, 295 tone-responsive cells from eight animals).
outcomes.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 2; Figure 1f
outcomes.quote: we also observed an inverse U relationship, where pure-tone response amplitudes are largest at baseline PDs that are within ... the intermediate range of an animal's PD [Fig. 1f, relative to maximum animal PD; p = 5.91 × 10−7, one-way Kruskal–Wallis test, 295 tone-responsive cells
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading (SD over time, responsive in both contrasts, peak window 2-2.8 s, maximum of the averaged trace) 318 cells are tone-responsive, within 295 plus or minus 29.5; the other inclusion readings give 339, 215 and 241. Peak responses differ across the seven bins (Kruskal-Wallis H = 51.83, p = 2.0e-09), largest in the 21-32% bin (15.88% dF/F) against 8.12 in the lowest and 13.08 in the highest. All 32 readings give p from 1.0e-10 to 7.3e-08 and the same top bin. Under the other cleanings and without the ZnT3-WT mouse AA0335 the main reading gives p = 2.8e-10 to 3.2e-06 with an interior top bin. The bins are not independent of mouse; the lowest bin holds cells of three mice. No trial is below 10% of animal max, so the two bin-1 readings are the same.
deviations: Group A is the ten mice the files label pupilPTinContrast (four F, six M, one ZnT3-WT), where the paper gives eight C57BL6/J mice (four F, four M); CTRL trials of the CGC assay are used. Keeping the ZnT3-WT mouse AA0335, as the label does, is an assumption; the fig2b-evoked-pd-whole-drc and fig3b-lme-coefficients outcomes rest on it, and group A without AA0335 is a variant in the notebook.

Pupil cleaning (assumption). The files hold the pupil radius with dropped frames and tracking failures (up to 1.5e6 pixels); the Methods' single pass (6 SD outliers of the first derivative) leaves these in, so a Hampel spike filter was added, the derivative step repeated, trials with more than half their frames missing dropped, and trials whose raw trace steps by more than a factor 2 between tracked frames dropped (118 of 2113 trials; a pupil does not double or halve its radius in 100 ms). The last step was added after the first verification round, because runs of tracking failures in AA0319 and AA0334 set their maxima. This sets each animal's maximum PD, hence baseline PD in % of maximum and the 50% selection. The rule reads the raw trace, before the spike filter, so it drops trials in 15 mice, not only AA0319 and AA0334, including trials whose only fault is a spike the filter removes; counted after the spike filter it drops 39 trials in 6 mice and gives the same animal maxima. The round-1 cleaning, the single pass and the narrower step rule are shown as variants in the notebook.

outcomes.notes: The mean high-contrast trace peaks 10.49% above baseline in ZnT3-WT after ZX1 (67 trials) and 11.17% in ZnT3-KO CTRL (47 trials; 10.93 with ZX1 pooled), all within 10 plus or minus 2.5. The WT CTRL high-contrast peak (13.23) is outside the interval, but WT low contrast (9.76 and 10.01) falls inside it, so the measure separates conditions only in part. The statement's second part (both contrasts resemble low contrast) is not tested by the criterion; fig4-wt-posthoc covers it and was partially reproduced.
deviations: Pupil cleaning (assumption). The files hold the pupil radius with dropped frames and tracking failures (up to 1.5e6 pixels); the Methods' single pass (6 SD outliers of the first derivative) leaves these in, so a Hampel spike filter was added, the derivative step repeated, trials with more than half their frames missing dropped, and trials whose raw trace steps by more than a factor 2 between tracked frames dropped (118 of 2113 trials; a pupil does not double or halve its radius in 100 ms). The last step was added after the first verification round, because runs of tracking failures in AA0319 and AA0334 set their maxima. This sets each animal's maximum PD, hence baseline PD in % of maximum and the 50% selection. The rule reads the raw trace, before the spike filter, so it drops trials in 15 mice, not only AA0319 and AA0334, including trials whose only fault is a spike the filter removes; counted after the spike filter it drops 39 trials in 6 mice and gives the same animal maxima. The round-1 cleaning, the single pass and the narrower step rule are shown as variants in the notebook.

Contrast of a DRC trial without the tone is that of its first 10 s; the files' DRCs switch contrast after 10 s (50-60 to 40-70 dB or the reverse), which the paper does not describe. The analysed 0 to 2 s lie in the first block.

findings.statement: The widefield imaging of Figure 5 (three mice with a cannula in the left auditory cortex, before and after contralateral and ipsilateral ZX1, with red-channel images) is not in the dandiset, so the three Figure 5 claims cannot be tested.

The pupil radius series hold tracking failures, single frames and runs at 3 to 1e6 times the pupil size, often next to dropped frames (68 trials have a maximum above three times their median; 118 trials step by more than a factor 2 between consecutive tracked frames). In AA0319 and AA0334 the failures also come as runs at a second level (130 to 160 against a pupil of about 25) that a spike filter does not remove. The DeepLabCut points and likelihoods that the Methods use to drop frames are not deposited, and the Methods' single derivative pass does not remove these failures, so each animal's maximum PD, and every baseline in % of maximum, depends on how they are cleaned.

Every pupil_radius series's description names one TwoPhotonSeries (the file's last, for example TwoPhotonSeries_036), not its own; the series can be matched to its trial only through the .tif file named in its comments.
25 pupil series attached to DRC trials have the length of a mapping trial (1430 samples) or an LED trial (300 samples) in place of twice the trial's 170 frames, in seven files.

In the stimulus table, starting_time is wrong by 24 h for 84 trials in seven files (AA0318, AA0319, AA0320, AA0322, AA0327, AA0330, AA0333). Trials recorded before the reference .tif have starting times near 86400 s, where the .tif creation times show they came minutes earlier. The pupil and fluorescence series take the same starting times.

The DRCs without a tone in the files (pulseSets PC_contrastChange) are 10 s of one contrast followed by 10 s of the other. The paper describes the sound-evoked pupil stimuli as low- or high-contrast DRCs and does not mention the switch.

Group sizes in the files differ from the paper. The files label ten mice pupilPTinContrast (four F, six M, one ZnT3-WT), where the paper gives eight C57BL6/J mice (four F, four M) for Figures 1 to 3. The pupil_contrast_ZnT3WT label holds five F and five M, where the paper gives six F and four M. Twelve mice have CGC-assay trials before and after ZX1 (two of them ZnT3-KO), where the paper gives fourteen C57BL6/J mice for Fig. 2d, e.

No label identifies the mice of Fig. 2d, e, and the FRA mapping trials used to select cells are in only 7 of 30 files. Whether the RoiResponseSeries are neuropil-corrected is not stated (unit lumens, description 'motion corrected ROIs'). The pupil radius has unit 'na' and no spatial scale.

Question for the authors on Fig. 2c. Which mice (the eight of Figs. 1-3, the fourteen of Fig. 2d, e, or both) and which unit (trials or per-mouse means) does the Wilcoxon rank sum test use? Pooled trials of both groups give p = 0.011, each group alone p = 0.099 and 0.16.

Question for the authors on Fig. 4c, d, f. What is the exact fixed-effect formula (the written formula has no contrast by treatment term, which the Results report), and is the coding reference or effects? In ZnT3-KO mice the contrast slope term is significant under three of four readings and not under the fourth.

Question for the authors on the GCA weights. How are the time polynomials scaled? With unit-norm orthogonal polynomials over the 21 samples from 0 to 2 s the ZnT3-WT ZX1 slope weight is -4.12 to -8.24, against the reported -1.41.
Question for the authors on the pupil cleaning. How were frames with tracking failures handled beyond the 6 SD derivative step? This sets each animal's maximum PD and the 50% selection.

Question for the authors on the Methods' correlation (r(624) = -0.35). Which trials does it use? No group and trial set here matches both counts (626 and 384); the closest, the mice labelled pupilBaseline_vs_evoked with DRC trials before and after ZX1, has 563 and 330, and r = -0.277. The same question holds for Fig. 6c (240 responses).

disagreements.reason: The notebook marks this blocked, but its own criterion can be evaluated. The KO ZX1 slope has p = 0.20 to 0.52 in all 4 readings. Neither weight is within tolerance, KO -0.55 to -3.1 against -0.64, WT -3.8 to -7.7 against -1.41.

Both slopes are positive with p < 1e-15. The ZX1 slopes (0.12 to 0.19) lie within the paper's ZX1 CI. But the ACSF slope is 0.326 (CI 0.28 to 0.37), above the paper's ACSF CI, and it overlaps no ZX1 CI. The criterion has no partial outcome; read strictly, this is not_reproduced.

The contrast slope is not significant in any reading, p = 0.07 for (a), 0.27 to 0.83 for (b). In reading (b), the within-ACSF HIGH-LOW contrast has p = 0.37. Only reading (b) has a row count (2604) that matches the df.

entries.name: 001256-cody-2024
entries.title: Cortical zinc and sound-contrast pupil responses (Cody, Kumar and Tzounopoulos 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Cody, Kumar and Tzounopoulos (2024) on dandiset 001256, which holds two-photon imaging of auditory cortex and pupillometry in 30 mice during low- and high-contrast sound, before and after ZX1 or ACSF, in C57BL6/J, ZnT3-WT and ZnT3-KO mice. It tests how pure-tone responses and contrast gain control vary with baseline pupil size, whether evoked pupil responses depend on contrast and on cortical zinc, and the controls of Figure 6. The widefield experiments of Figure 5 are not in the dandiset.
